- [HTTP-001] **Control-plane security-hook composition** — `packages/control-plane/app.ts` composes version/sigil/request-ID/logging, lease and Origin admission, early mounts, standard authentication, provenance gating, access recording, error handlers, and routes. Client-controlled method, URL, headers, and body cross different Elysia hook scopes; do early returns, parse failures, plugin deduplication, and routes registered before global hooks receive the intended admission and response protections?
- [HTTP-002] **Control-plane authentication GET forwarder** — `GET /api/auth/*` in `packages/control-plane/app.ts` delegates through `forwardBetterAuth`; the path, cookies, credential headers, and implicit `HEAD` request are untrusted. Audit blocked/disabled-path matching, trusted client-IP and request-ID stamping, pre-admission ordering, redirect/header preservation, and unread GET-body handling at this forwarding boundary.
- [HTTP-003] **Control-plane authentication POST forwarder** — `POST /api/auth/*` in `packages/control-plane/app.ts` uses `parse: 'none'` before the ordinary auth plugin. Caller-controlled content type, body, path, and cookies enter library/ceremony parsing; are path refusals and the library budget applied before expensive work, and do every pre-parse refusal, bounded-read handoff, and re-emitted response preserve status, cookies, security headers, and connection-close semantics?
- [HTTP-004] **SCIM GET forwarding boundary** — `GET /scim/v2/*` in `packages/control-plane/app.ts` calls the standalone mount through `forwardScim`, before standard authentication. Audit untrusted path/header handling, disabled-mount 404s, implicit `HEAD`, original-request peer resolution, overwritten internal forwarding headers, and isolation from the interactive credential namespace and failure budget; SCIM resource semantics remain downstream of this boundary.
- [HTTP-005] **SCIM POST forwarding boundary** — `POST /scim/v2/*` in `packages/control-plane/app.ts`, with body admission in `packages/control-plane/scim-mount.ts`, forwards raw caller bytes under `parse: 'none'`. Does the parent enforce its cap before standalone parsing, preserve the trustworthy peer after request reconstruction, and close unread bodies on disabled-mount, cap, and routing refusals without falling into interactive authentication?
- [HTTP-006] **SCIM PUT forwarding boundary** — `PUT /scim/v2/*` in `packages/control-plane/app.ts` shares the parent-to-standalone forwarding mechanism. Audit declared versus delivered body length, media-type handling, method preservation, and refusal/header propagation so an attacker-controlled replacement request cannot escape the standalone mount's admission or consume the ordinary auth budget.
- [HTTP-007] **SCIM PATCH forwarding boundary** — `PATCH /scim/v2/*` in `packages/control-plane/app.ts` forwards through the same pre-auth body cap in `packages/control-plane/scim-mount.ts`. Audit chunked/absent-length bodies, preservation of PATCH across request reconstruction, parse failures, and local error-hook ownership before downstream patch interpretation.
- [HTTP-008] **SCIM DELETE forwarding boundary** — `DELETE /scim/v2/*` in `packages/control-plane/app.ts` is explicitly `parse: 'none'`. Client-sent bodies and unsupported paths can reach a nominally bodyless operation; do the parent cap, standalone refusal, 204 re-emission, and connection-close handling remain correct without borrowing session or `sdp_` authority?
- [HTTP-009] **Fact-push pre-standard-auth mount isolation** — `packages/control-plane/app.ts` mounts `packages/control-plane/routes/fact-push.ts` before session-tier and standard authentication. Caller-supplied `sdf_`, `sds_`, `sdp_`, cookies, and malformed credential headers cross this namespace boundary; verify local parser/limiter/error/security-header ownership and that plugin propagation cannot authenticate or charge the request through an unintended credential system.
- [HTTP-010] **Session-only tier placement** — `packages/control-plane/routes/session-tier.ts` is mounted before standard authentication in `packages/control-plane/app.ts`. Cookie-bearing requests to workspace selection, identity notifications, and invitations do not acquire the ordinary `AuthContext`; audit inherited Origin admission and header-credential handling, especially the assumption that a presented credential makes a request safe to exempt from cookie-CSRF checks.
- [HTTP-011] **Control-plane trusted-publishing mutation gate** — `packages/control-plane/trusted-publishing-token-gate.ts` globally refuses authenticated trusted-publishing tokens on methods outside `GET`/`HEAD`/`OPTIONS`; `packages/shared/universal/token-origin-enforcement-points.test.ts` pins adjacency to the auth plugin. Audit method normalization, inherited transform ordering, parse-stage failures, and every earlier mount's inability to authenticate this credential before the gate.
- [HTTP-012] **Control-plane lease admission before routing** — `packages/control-plane/lease-admission.ts` and `packages/control-plane/app.ts` gate all non-health traffic on the injected holder status. The client controls the pathname and method used against `isLeaseAdmissionExemptPath`; examine `/health` versus the whole `/health/` subtree, encoded/dot/slash variants, unavailable status, direct/internal traffic, and the gate's own error, security-header, and unread-body behavior.
- [HTTP-013] **Standby-to-holder listener handoff** — `packages/control-plane/standby-health.ts` and `packages/control-plane/index.ts` expose a health-only app before the full app takes the port. Requests can race startup, takeover, and shutdown; does readiness become true only after the protected full listener exists, and can any old listener, omitted injected gate, or different hook set serve application traffic during the handoff?
- [HTTP-014] **HTTP transport parsing before application hooks** — `packages/control-plane/app.ts` and `packages/registry-api/app.ts` configure Bun/Elysia listeners rather than parse raw HTTP themselves. Attackers supply request-target forms, duplicate or conflicting `Host`/`Content-Length`/`Transfer-Encoding` headers, malformed methods, and oversized headers; establish the pinned transport's rejection and normalization behavior, its agreement with a reverse proxy, and which rejections bypass all application logging and headers.

Audit `OPTIONS /api/v1/*`, `/api/auth/*`, and `/scim/v2/*` with caller-selected Origin and requested headers: what actually answers, which hooks run, and can a proxy-added preflight policy or method override expose cookie-authenticated operations beyond the configured origin contract?
- [HTTP-016] **Control-plane GET catch-all namespace boundary** — `GET /*` in `packages/control-plane/routes/spa.ts`, mounted last by `packages/control-plane/app.ts`, handles otherwise-unmatched paths. Audit client-controlled encoded paths, bare namespace roots, static/parameter/wildcard precedence, and `isExcludedPath` coverage so API, internal, SCIM, health, OpenAPI, and registry-protocol requests receive the intended miss rather than an accidental successful SPA response.
- [HTTP-017] **Control-plane catch-all HEAD behavior** — implicit `HEAD /*` reaches the GET wildcard in `packages/control-plane/routes/spa.ts`, whose method check returns 404. Audit how this differs from implicit HEAD on explicit API/probe routes, whether the body is stripped without losing refusal headers, and how client-declared HEAD bodies are closed on this path.
- [HTTP-018] **Registry shell lifecycle ordering** — `createRegistryHttpShell` in `packages/registry-api/app.ts` installs logging/auth/access plugins, ingress stamping, declared-size refusal, stream wrapping, and parent-first error translation. Attacker-controlled requests can fail at every stage; do onRequest hooks run before parsing and auth, do wrappers reach all subsequent handlers, and do scoped/global hook inheritance and early raw responses preserve the intended shell?
- [HTTP-019] **Shared registry runtime security state** — `packages/registry-api/registry-runtime.ts` owns the authentication-failure limiter, anonymous limiter, trusted-proxy set, and service dependencies shared by composed apps. - [HTTP-020] **Namespaced registry route membership** — `createNamespacedRegistryApp` in `packages/registry-api/app.ts` mounts root/probes/metrics/search and ecosystem barrels; `packages/registry-api/lib/logical-route-coverage.test.ts` checks actual registrations. Client paths such as `/health`, `/metrics`, `/api/v1/search`, and another ecosystem prefix are protocol coordinates or misses here; verify that no operations/management handler or foreign format leaks into any native composition, including literal-prefix mounts.

- [HTTP-024] **Literal native mount derivation** — `packages/registry-api/lib/composition-profile.ts` derives an Elysia prefix through `listenerMountPath` in `packages/types/exposed/repository-endpoint.ts`. Persisted endpoint configuration crosses into route syntax while the client controls the incoming path; verify literal-path admission, root-versus-prefix handling, Docker's fixed `/v2`, intact proxy forwarding, and agreement between matching, stripping, and outward canonical addresses.
- [HTTP-025] **Namespaced pre-routing ecosystem classification** — `classifyNamespaced` in `packages/registry-api/lib/ingress-classifier.ts` delegates prefix recognition to `ecosystemFromPath` in `packages/registry-api/lib/http-response.ts`. Audit raw pathname case, percent-encoding, trailing slash, doubled separators, dot normalization, and near-prefix spellings so body limits, credential selection, and error envelopes agree with the route Bun/Elysia ultimately dispatches.
- [HTTP-026] **Native pre-routing ecosystem classification** — `packages/registry-api/lib/ingress-classifier.ts` selects the bound format only within `isWithinListenerMount`. A client controls mount lookalikes and nested `/v2/` or fenced paths; verify segment-boundary comparisons and decoder agreement, that another format cannot activate its verifier/limit/envelope, and that paths outside the mount receive the explicitly unclassified treatment.
- [HTTP-027] **Operations pre-routing classification** — `packages/registry-api/lib/ingress-classifier.ts` classifies every operations path as repository-free with no exchange or stateless verifier. - [HTTP-028] **Physical-to-logical route identity** — `packages/registry-api/lib/request-logical-route.ts` and `packages/shared/universal/registry-logical-routes.ts` map method plus Elysia's matched template, not a client path guess. - [HTTP-029] **Automatic HEAD and explicit HEAD dispatch** — `packages/shared/universal/registry-logical-routes.ts`, `packages/registry-api/lib/router-behavior.test.ts`, and `packages/registry-api/lib/composite-elysia-behavior.test.ts` pin HEAD fallback, raw wildcard captures, decoded named parameters, and wildcard/hybrid HEAD body draining. - [HTTP-030] **Registry OPTIONS and unsupported-method dispatch** — `packages/registry-api/app.ts`, `packages/registry-api/native-app.ts`, `packages/registry-api/operations-app.ts`, and `packages/shared/universal/registry-logical-routes.ts` determine the method-specific route population. - [HTTP-031] **Whole-registration admission coverage** — `packages/registry-api/lib/pre-resolver-admission-sites.ts` and `packages/registry-api/lib/pre-resolver-admission-guardian.test.ts` require real resolution/dispatch hook markers or a classified pre-resolver row. - [HTTP-032] **Public repository addressing selection** — `packages/registry-api/lib/composition-profile.ts` and `packages/registry-api/lib/resolve-repository.ts` distinguish path selectors from pinned bound selectors and enforce `admitsPublicAddressing`. - [HTTP-034] **Invalid-credential versus credential-free anonymous admission** — `resolveAnonymousRepository` in `packages/registry-api/lib/resolve-repository.ts` consumes `presentedCredential` from `packages/shared/server/auth-middleware.ts`. Audit empty/unrecognized credential headers, failed tokens, and the explicitly already-verified synthetic-credential exception; can any invalid presented credential be treated as absent, or private/unknown/wrong-layout targets be distinguished before anonymous eligibility is established?
- [HTTP-035] **Synthesized anonymous authorization context** — `packages/shared/server/anonymous-auth.ts` creates a truthy context with sentinel IDs, `role: 'entitlement'`, repository scope, no duties, and no global-admin authority; `packages/registry-api/lib/resolve-repository.ts` replaces the earlier null auth. - [HTTP-036] **Per-repository anonymous request budget** — `packages/registry-api/lib/anonymous-rate-limit.ts` and `packages/registry-api/registry-runtime.ts` use a required repository-ID bucket and a budget-plus-one construction. Audit exact boundary counts, cache-hit charging, shared starvation, cross-replica multiplication, unknown/private target non-charging, and once-per-window telemetry; can anonymous requests avoid the budget or spend another repository's bucket?
- [HTTP-037] **Authentication-presence guard** — `requireAuth` in `packages/shared/server/auth-middleware.ts` tests the context's truthy `auth` field and throws 401. Audit that only trusted derives can populate it and callers do not confuse presence with a DB-backed principal, valid role, object scope, or deployment authority; admitted anonymous and entitlement contexts intentionally satisfy this primitive.
- [HTTP-038] **Control-plane base-context sigil** — `packages/control-plane/context.ts` stamps a module-private Symbol and `assertBaseContext` checks its presence. - [HTTP-039] **Control-plane identity-tier assertion** — `assertIdentityContext` in `packages/control-plane/context.ts` additionally checks for `sessionIdentity`. Audit the trusted derive that owns that key and use on pre-standard-auth routes: can a token-derived or merely key-present context be mistaken for a resolved browser identity when cookies and credential headers are mixed?
- [HTTP-040] **Control-plane workspace-tier assertion** — `assertWorkspaceContext` in `packages/control-plane/context.ts` requires workspace keys after the base sigil. - [HTTP-041] **Control-plane repository-tier assertion** — `assertRepoContext` in `packages/control-plane/context.ts` requires repository keys after workspace narrowing. Audit consistency between resolved repository, workspace, slug, and credential restrictions, and whether route composition can provide keys without running the owning resolver or subsequent object-privilege guard.
- [HTTP-042] **Registry base-context sigil and decorations** — `packages/registry-api/context.ts` and `packages/registry-api/app.ts` establish the registry-only sigil and trusted runtime decorations. - [HTTP-043] **Concrete registry context narrowing** — `assertRegistryRepoContext` in `packages/registry-api/context.ts` checks that the resolved row has a concrete hosting mode. - [HTTP-044] **Wide principal-route registry context** — `assertRegistryPrincipalRouteContext` in `packages/registry-api/context.ts` deliberately permits composite rows for diagnostics and principal-state routes. - [HTTP-045] **Error-lifecycle context narrowing** — `getErrorContext` and `isFullAuthContext` in `packages/shared/server/errors.ts` recover plugin fields after partial execution. Audit malformed or incompletely derived auth values, missing request IDs before parsing, and the shallow universal guard: can error rendering misattribute an actor, dereference absent authority fields, or throw a second error that discards the intended refusal?
- [HTTP-046] **Verified-token to request-authority mapping** — `mapVerifiedTokenToAuthContext` in `packages/shared/server/auth-middleware.ts` copies the contract from `packages/shared/server/auth-types.ts`. - [HTTP-047] **Control-plane lookup enrichment boundary** — `controlPlaneTokenLookup` in `packages/control-plane/app.ts` wraps verification, usage tracking, and cached duty resolution. - [HTTP-048] **Registry lookup telemetry boundary** — the lookup in `packages/registry-api/app.ts` verifies on the read handle and launches usage/first-use work through `writerDb` and `requestWork`. - [HTTP-049] **Credential-header presence contract** — `CREDENTIAL_HEADER_NAMES` and `hasCredentialHeader` in `packages/shared/server/token-extraction.ts` are shared by malformed-auth accounting, anonymous admission, Origin exemptions, and cache variation. - [HTTP-054] **X-NuGet-ApiKey extraction** — `packages/shared/server/token-extraction.ts` provides a separate NuGet header fallback with prefix/length checks. Audit case-insensitive header retrieval, duplicate values, invalid higher-priority credentials, and consistency with anonymous denial and `Vary` so this alternate channel cannot authenticate or cache a response under another channel's assumptions.
- [HTTP-055] **Mixed credential-header precedence** — `extractToken` in `packages/shared/server/token-extraction.ts` falls through extraction branches, while `packages/shared/server/token-extraction.test.ts` pins valid-header precedence. - [HTTP-056] **Header-token versus session fallback** — `makeAuthPlugin` in `packages/shared/server/auth-middleware.ts` attempts session resolution when no raw token was extracted and returns null auth after failed token verification. - [HTTP-057] **Opt-in stateless credential verifier seam** — `packages/shared/server/auth-types.ts`, `packages/shared/server/auth-middleware.ts`, and `packages/registry-api/app.ts` define `AuthContext`/null/undefined outcomes and profile-selected applicability. - [HTTP-062] **Consume-before-verification authentication limiter** — `packages/shared/server/auth-middleware.ts` uses `RateLimiter.recordAttempt` from `packages/shared/server/rate-limiter.ts` before verifier work. - [HTTP-072] **Fresh privilege-resolution option forwarding** — `packages/shared/server/privilege-guards.ts`, `packages/control-plane/routes/shared/principals.ts`, and `packages/registry-api/lib/auth.ts` map `fresh` to `skipCache` and forward operation metadata.
